newsitem.title: UK: EU seen awarding up to 90,000 T sugar at tender.
newsitem.headline: EU seen awarding up to 90,000 T sugar at tender.

text.p: The European Union (EU) is expected to award as much as 90,000 tonnes of current series white sugar at its weekly tender later on Wednesday, traders said.
The recent widening of the nearby March/May spread could encourage a higher tonnage in licence applications, aided by the strength in the dollar against other European currencies, they said.
The Paris market, used by the EU to price its restitution calculation, saw solid hedge selling during Tuesday's session, which suggested a higher tonnage.
"The March/May has widened out, which means you can get restitutions against May and hedge them against March," said one.

"The dollar strengthened overnight, which further improves the position of traders looking to take licences," he added, forecasting tonnage at a minimum 60,000 tonnes and possibly as high as 90,000 tonnes.
Last week the EU awarded a total 22,750 tonnes of current series white sugar at its tender.
"It depends how quick off the mark people were and how far they trust the market to allow them to hedge."
But another trader was more cautious due to the actual reported amounts of quota sugar being traded and said 40,000 tonnes might be a more realistic volume.
"From a dollar and market point of view it's not a bad week to take licences," he said.
But traders agreed in their forecast for this week's maximum restitution level, estimating 44.787 Ecus (European currency units) per 100 kilos of sugar after the 45.519 Ecus awarded last week.
Licences are currently valid until the end of July.
